scope: Theorem 13.26 (Weighted realization and simultaneous numerical readings) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 145. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix any bounded support size for the comparisons and any desired fixed number of spare copies. There are absolute initial cohort-stock and marker-loss bounds, independent of the numerical unit sizes and the number of cohorts, with the following property. The bounds may depend on the fixed support and spare-copy requirements. An ordinary realization of a nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation and with top order M, gives a forward realization after at most that many marker deletions, with all cuts product in an actual alternating power. A single common cell alignment gives positive sizes uj ≤ M, equal on each cohort and one on all surviving markers. In this same alignment the equal-total reading of Proposition 13.24 and the square reading of Theorem 13.25 hold. If the input is a finite algebra of size m representing a nontrivial image, the same conclusion holds with M = 60mm!, for a possibly different nontrivial image of the original template. The full template itself is finitely representable.
